decisive_moments.reason: Pro correctly distinguishes trust and governability from raw reliability or cost, and gives a plausible production-oriented case for bounded permissions, blast-radius reduction, and independent auditing.

Con identifies the central burden-of-proof problem: the pro case depends on enforceable boundaries, while coordination, semantic mismatch, correlated errors, and orchestrator failures can undermine whole-system trust.
Con directly reframes the comparison around end-to-end outcomes and explains why the stated advantages of teams may be domain-conditional rather than generally applicable.

flags.quote: Thus the qualified, comparative conjecture stands: bounded teams are generally easier to govern and trust
The missing condition is not fatal—it identifies the engineering test
A general agent’s single context can be more reliable on novel, cross-domain tasks
